translation_notes: two graph.add((s, p, o)) calls merged into one `assertion += g{ ... . ... }` island

prefix declared for nanopub.namespaces.HYCL (namespaces.HYCL.claims -> hycl:claims); the dc/rdf/dcterms/prov/xsd prefixes the draft declared are unused in this region and were dropped (they had also been spliced into the middle of a `from ... import (` statement, which does not parse)

IMPORTANT negative finding: BNode('test')/BNode('test2') must stay Python interpolations `{BNode("test")}`. Writing `_:test`/`_:test2` inside the island is syntactically fine but changes the result: island labels are fresh at every evaluation, and nanopub's trusty artifact code is a hash over the concrete blank-node identifiers, so the expected code RA-1eE8scf... becomes RAfggp5u... (verified). The `_:{expr}` data-keyed form does not help either, since its identity is derived, not the literal label

context (driver-side, identical for both representations): the nanopub package is not installed in the venv, so the corpus checkout Nanopublication/nanopub-py@05022dc4bc is put on sys.path before either module is executed

context shim: `from tests.conftest import ...` -> `from conftest_context import ...` (same names). Upstream conftest downloads the nanopub test suite at import time just to get the rsa-key1 pair and pings the nanopub server; the shim copies that key pair from Nanopublication/nanopub-testsuite@main (MIT) into the example directory and keeps the profile/NanopubConf definitions verbatim

the driver's equivalence check is strong despite the region returning None: `assert expected_trusty in np.source_uri` is a hash over the signed nanopub, so any difference in the assertion graph fails the run
